prompt: Ana deleted pod `web-768c88b7c7-5dbxj`. Two seconds later the ReplicaSet still had three pods. What happened?
hint: Compare the names before and after.

choices.text: The deletion was refused because the pod had an owner
choices.why: `5dbxj` is gone from the second listing; the deletion went through.

choices.text: A new pod was made from the template
choices.why: Right: `5xvw2`, with a new name, because the count had dropped to two.

choices.text: The kubelet restarted the same pod under its old name
choices.why: A deleted pod is gone for good; the replacement has a different name.

choices.text: The Deployment restored the pod from etcd's history
choices.why: Nothing is restored; a new object is created from the template, with a new address too.

prompt: After Ana relabelled one pod `app=debug`, there were four pods and the ReplicaSet reported three. What is the fourth?
hint: Which selector does it still answer?

choices.text: A replacement that will be removed in a minute
choices.why: The new pod `l7mxz` is the one that counts; nothing will remove it.

choices.text: A pod the ReplicaSet will delete to get back to three
choices.why: It no longer matches the selector, so the ReplicaSet does not see it at all.

choices.text: An orphan nobody counts, replaces or deletes
choices.why: Right. It keeps running outside every selector, which is useful in an incident and a hazard by accident.

choices.text: A second ReplicaSet's pod
choices.why: Only one ReplicaSet existed then, and the pod belongs to none.

prompt: A Service selects `app: web`. Ana relabels a misbehaving pod `app=debug` during an incident. What does that buy her?
hint: Two selectors stop seeing the pod at once.

choices.text: Nothing, since the pod keeps running
choices.why: Running is the point: it is out of rotation but still there to inspect.

choices.text: A restart of the pod with fresh memory
choices.why: Nothing restarts it; its state is exactly what she wants to keep.

choices.text: Its deletion, once the ReplicaSet notices
choices.why: The ReplicaSet stops seeing it and so never deletes it.

choices.text: No traffic reaches it, a replacement takes its place, and its state stays inspectable
choices.why: Right. The Service and the ReplicaSet both select by label, so both let go of it at once.

prompt: `kubectl set image deployment/web shop=shop:1.1` left two ReplicaSets. Which one wants the pods?

choices.text: Both, two each
choices.why: The old one went to 0; the Deployment moved the count across.

choices.text: The old one, until somebody deletes the new one
choices.why: It is the reverse: the new one wants 2 and the old one 0.

choices.text: The new one, `web-798bdd9498`, with 2
choices.why: Right. The old one is kept empty for a rollback.

choices.text: Neither: the Deployment holds the pods directly
choices.why: A Deployment never owns pods; it owns ReplicaSets.

prompt: Why does a Deployment make a second ReplicaSet for a new image instead of editing the first one?
hint: What would an edited ReplicaSet do with the pods it already has?

choices.text: A ReplicaSet's template cannot be edited at all
choices.why: It can be; editing it just does nothing to existing pods.

choices.text: The old pods still match, so it would leave them all as they are
choices.why: Right. A ReplicaSet only counts; a second one with a new hash is how the pods actually change.

choices.text: Two ReplicaSets make the update faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason; the pace is set by the strategy (lesson 35).

choices.text: The API server forbids two images in one ReplicaSet
choices.why: A pod template can hold several containers with different images.

prompt: Ana deleted every ReplicaSet of `web`. What did the next listing show, six seconds later?

choices.text: No ReplicaSets and no pods
choices.why: The Deployment noticed the missing ReplicaSet and made it again.

choices.text: `web-798bdd9498` again, wanting 2 pods
choices.why: Right: the same name, because the template and so its hash had not changed.

choices.text: Both ReplicaSets back, with their history
choices.why: Only the one it needs was made; the old empty one was not.

choices.text: A ReplicaSet with a new random name
choices.why: The name comes from the template's hash, not from chance.

prompt: A Deployment adds the label `pod-template-___` to each ReplicaSet's selector, so it counts only pods made from that template.
hint: It is a short digest of the template.

prompt: Match each object with what it does.

pairs.right: Makes one ReplicaSet per template and moves the count between them
Makes or deletes pods until the count of matching ones is right
Runs the containers, on one node

right_distractors: Chooses the node each pod runs on

prompt: Which of these would leave pods running that no controller counts? Choose all that apply.
hint: Think about the selector, never the name.

choices.text: Changing a running pod's `app` label by hand
choices.why: Right: it drops out of the selector and becomes an orphan.

choices.text: Deleting a pod
choices.why: That pod is gone, and its replacement is counted.

choices.text: Scaling the Deployment to zero
choices.why: That deletes the pods rather than stranding them.

choices.text: Creating a bare pod with no labels
choices.why: Right: no selector ever matched it, so nothing counts or replaces it (lesson 9).

choices.text: Changing the Deployment's image
choices.why: The old pods are replaced by the new ReplicaSet's.
